answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, while attestations are linked by timing, keys, and stake provenance. If k identities coordinate equivocation, their aggregate penalty scales as O(k^2), making correlated fraud costlier than isolated faults. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation and an exponential capital-loss multiplier across the sybil swarm, so recycled stake cannot cheaply restore control. The rule applies equally to a sonnet, crystal, or glacier-themed identity.
